name: Mambassa
description: Mambassa is a lively Italian card game played on the coast of the Marche province. It is a four-card variant of Petrangola (also known as 31), where players aim to collect cards of high value in a single suit, with a maximum of 41 points. The game features a unique 'monte' (table cards) exchange mechanic and knocking system similar to Schwimmen.

history.origins: Played on the coast of the Italian province of Marche. The name 'Mambassa' is of uncertain origin but the game is essentially a four-card version of Petrangola.
timeline: Traditional: Played in coastal Marche region
Related: Derived from Petrangola, which is related to Schwimmen/31
Present: Remains a regional favorite in central Italy
history.cultural: A social game played in cafes and family gatherings in the Marche region, often for small stakes.
history.evolution: Developed as a four-card variant of the three-card Petrangola, increasing the maximum hand value from 31 to 41.

setup.players: 3-8 players (optimal with 5-6). Each player starts with 4 tokens (vite/lives).
setup.deck: 40-card Italian-suited Piacentine deck. Rank: Ace (11), King (10), Horse (10), Jack (10), 7, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2 (face value). No 8s, 9s, or 10s.
setup.dealing: 4 cards face down to each player. Dealer looks at next 4 cards and either places them face up as the 'monte' or takes them as a hand (which counts as a knock).
setup.equipment: 40-card Italian Piacentine deck; tokens (four per player, one agreed value).

rules.objective: Have the highest total value in one suit (maximum 41) or collect a 'mambassa' (four equal cards or four-card sequence). Avoid having the lowest hand when someone knocks.
rules.gameplay: Player to dealer's right begins; play passes anticlockwise. Each player may exchange 0, 1, 2, 3 or all 4 hand cards for an equal number from the face-up monte; if they did not exchange all 4 they may optionally discard one card face down to the bottom of the stock and draw the top card. Exchanging all 4 or exchanging none and not drawing counts as a knock; after a knock each other player has one more turn, then hands are exposed and compared.
keyRules: Each turn: exchange 0–4 cards with the monte, then optionally discard one to bottom of stock and draw one from top. Exchanging all 4 or exchanging 0 and not drawing counts as a knock. After a knock, each other player has one more turn. Lowest hand(s) pay one token to the pool. Four Aces (Mambassa) or Quarantuna (41 in one suit) declared immediately ends the hand with special payouts.

strategy.basic: Focus on building a strong hand in one suit. The maximum is 41 (Ace + King + Horse + Jack of the same suit). Don't hold onto weak cards hoping they'll improve.
strategy.intermediate: Watch what cards other players take from the monte - this reveals what suits they're building. If you see someone take a Coin card, they likely have other Coin cards in hand.
strategy.advanced: The dealer has a significant advantage by seeing the monte first. As dealer, consider taking the monte as your hand if it's strong - this immediately knocks and limits other players to one exchange. Timing your knock is crucial - knock early with a good hand to prevent opponents from improving.
tips: Four equal cards (especially low ones like 2-2-2-2) are very strong hands
Sequences are harder to complete but beat three-of-a-kind hands
Pay attention to which cards have been exchanged - they're out of play
If you have three Aces, you're guaranteed not to lose (only four Aces beats you)
